title: Cognitive Ease
coreMove: Separate the feeling that a claim reads smoothly from the evidence that it is true, and treat fluency itself as a cue worth investigating rather than trusting.

exampleSpecs.domain: a cardiac nurse reviewing a handoff note printed in a crisp sans-serif versus a smudged carbon copy on the next patient
exampleSpecs.audience: a bedside nurse working the back half of a twelve-hour shift
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a medication reconciliation error gets caught before the next dose or silently carried forward
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the nurse catches herself weighting the legible note as more credible and forces herself to cross-check the smudged one against the chart rather than against her feeling about it

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal zoning board hearing where one developer's proposal rhymes in its bullet points and the other's does not
exampleSpecs.audience: a small-town zoning commissioner with no planning background
exampleSpecs.stakes: a twenty-year land-use decision that will shape a neighborhood the commissioner's grandchildren will live in
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the commissioner notices that the rhyming proposal is landing as more trustworthy and asks what specifically about its content, not its sound, would survive paraphrase

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook tasting a new supplier's stock against the restaurant's house stock during a Tuesday prep shift
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous chef deciding whether to switch vendors
exampleSpecs.stakes: food cost, consistency across a twelve-table dinner service, and the chef's credibility with the owner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the cook registers that the familiar stock feels right on the tongue in a way the new one does not, and isolates whether that is fluency of familiarity or actual flavor superiority before recommending

exampleSpecs.domain: a district court judge reading sentencing memos at the end of an afternoon docket
exampleSpecs.audience: a trial judge with twenty-six years on the bench
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether two defendants with similar facts receive similar sentences or are split by the mood the memos put the judge in
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the judge reconstructs, after the fact, how the easier-to-read memo produced a warmer impression of the defendant and asks what procedural countermeasure would have blocked that leakage

exampleSpecs.domain: a high-school orchestra director auditioning two clarinetists for first chair in a narrow practice room
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-school music teacher with a hundred-student program
exampleSpecs.stakes: the morale of a section that will notice any chair placement that tracks social comfort rather than playing
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director recognizes that the student who plays the familiar warm-up excerpt sounds 'more musical' partly because the excerpt is familiar to the director's ear, and redesigns the audition so repertoire novelty is equalized

exampleSpecs.domain: a grant reviewer working through the last four proposals of the evening against a submission deadline
exampleSpecs.audience: a tenured researcher serving on an NIH study section
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a first-time applicant's genuinely strong science is scored below a veteran's polished prose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the reviewer predicts her own scores before reading carefully, then reads and notices which proposals her prediction overrated on fluency alone, and adjusts her written critique to separate clarity of writing from quality of design
